core.title: Keep every scanned source file's maintainability index at or above 20
core.given: Any scanned (non-test, non-vendored, non-build) source file (the profile's source suffixes define 'source'; the never-scanned trees are the profile's stack-wide exclusion list)
core.when: its approximate SEI maintainability index is evaluated
core.then: The file MUST score at least 20 on the approximate SEI maintainability index.
prefer: Treat a low score as a sensor for accumulated responsibility; repair cohesion and ownership first. Before optimizing the score, diagnose: responsibilities changing for different reasons, decision-heavy regions and repeated logic dominating the file, missing design context.
Extract a cohesive responsibility into its own module with a clear ownership boundary.
Simplify genuinely complex or duplicated logic as part of that extraction.
Comment only real decisions or invariants.
avoid: Filler comments to improve the formula's comment term.
Splitting at an arbitrary line boundary or into tiny fragments solely to reduce LOC.
Moving complexity unchanged into a sibling module.
A generalized abstraction unrelated to the responsibilities already present.
unless: The file produces zero code lines after comment stripping (scores 100, never fails).
The file is a test file or in a vendored/build tree (outside the scan; the trees are the profile's stack-wide exclusion list, exact classification owned by the checker).
core.why: MI alone judges the whole FILE: a file can pass every per-function threshold yet be unmaintainable through accumulated size and operator density. 20 is deliberately low—below it nobody should be asked to modify the file—and since MI mixes size, branching, density and comments, gaming one term moves the number without making the module easier to change.
evidence: The stack's maintainability-metrics check no longer reports the triggering finding (score >= 20) for the file.
Fixing the finding creates no new length, complexity, duplication or dependency-flow violations.
Existing behavior and tests remain green after the refactor.
Each resulting module has a coherent reason to change.
Dependency direction remains consistent with the existing architecture.
The refactor introduces no new violations of the stack's ATDD conventions.
Diff review shows no filler comments, arbitrary line-boundary splits, or complexity moved unchanged into a sibling module.
verification: A repository-wide metrics check scores every scanned source file—changed or not, in every phase—and fails when a file's maintainability index falls below 20; the score is an approximation and is treated as one.

The metric is the approximate SEI maintainability index: MI = 171 - 5.2*ln(V) - 0.23*avgCC - 16.2*ln(LOC) + 50*sin(sqrt(2.4*CM)), clamped to the 0..100 range, where V is the operator/operand volume standing in for the file's information content, avgCC is the average decision density per function, CM is the comment ratio, and LOC is code lines; how each term is measured (AST, tokenizer or approximation) is the realization's choice.
A file producing zero code lines after comment stripping scores 100 and never fails.

Test files and the trees on the profile's stack-wide exclusion list are outside the scan; every other file with a source suffix is scanned regardless of whether it changed. The exact classification of the excluded trees is owned by the stack's checker.
Strict disposition: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline. Severity 2.

values: scanned source file: a file with the profile's source suffixes, in the scanned roots, that is neither a test file nor in a never-scanned (vendored/build) tree; every scanned file counts, changed or not, in every phase
maintainability-metrics check reports a scanned file below 20

fires: Any scanned source file, edited or untouched, scores below 20 on the approximate SEI maintainability index.
A source module has accumulated enough size, operator density and branching to score below 20, even though every function passes its own complexity/length thresholds.
The agent is working in or near a large source file that the metrics check flagged for a low score.
doesNotFire: A test file with a low score (test files are outside the scan).
A file in a vendored or build tree (never scanned).
A source file that is empty or contains only comments (zero code lines after comment stripping score 100).
A source file scoring 20 or more, even if imperfect.
A file that is not scanned source per the profile.

neutralityNotes: The obligation is stack-neutral and stays whole in the core: every scanned source file, changed or not, must score at least 20 on the approximate SEI maintainability index. The exact formula (171 - 5.2*ln(V) - 0.23*avgCC - 16.2*ln(LOC) + 50*sin(sqrt(2.4*CM)), clamped to 0..100) is neutral mathematics and is kept verbatim in core verification; what could NOT be made neutral is how the terms are measured — the Bun detector's regex approximation, no-AST/no-library approach and its ten-decimal cross-check against the python-pytest sibling are bunOnly. Which files are scanned comes from the profile (tooling.languages, suffix.source, roots.scan, roots.excluded); under the Bun profile the scan set is exactly every non-test, non-vendored, non-build TS/TSX file — no broader generated-source exclusion is added — and the checker owns the exact classification of excluded trees. Detector/validator/finding ids (bun_ts_metrics_detector) are bunOnly. 'ATDD Bun violations' was generalized to 'violations of the stack's ATDD conventions' — no obligation added or dropped.
